preconditions.description: Input must have n destinations (2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) and m corridors (n-1 ≤ m ≤ 10^6), where n is the number of nodes and m is the number of edges in the graph.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b and 0 <= e <= 10**9 for a, b, e in corridors)
preconditions.description: Each corridor is defined by two distinct destinations (1 ≤ a, b ≤ n, a ≠ b) and an energy requirement (0 ≤ e ≤ 10^9).

preconditions.expression: len(set((min(a, b), max(a, b)) for a, b, e in corridors)) == m
preconditions.description: No pair of destinations {a, b} repeats in the input (undirected edges are unique).
The graph formed by the corridors is connected (there exists a path between any two destinations).

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == m and all(0 <= e_max <= 10**9 for e_max in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Output contains exactly m integers, each representing E_max(c_i) for the i-th corridor, where 0 ≤ E_max(c_i) ≤ 10^9.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[i] == max_e(c_i, corridors) for i, c_i in enumerate(corridors))
postconditions.description: For each corridor c_i = (a_i, b_i, e_i), E_max(c_i) is the largest e ≤ 10^9 such that if the energy requirement of c_i were changed to e, then c_i would be part of some minimum spanning tree (MST) of the graph.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= e_max <= e_i or (e_max > e_i and is_in_mst(c_i, corridors, e_max)) for i, (a_i, b_i, e_i) in enumerate(corridors) for e_max in [output_lines[i]])
postconditions.description: If E_max(c_i) > e_i, then the corridor c_i must be part of at least one MST when its energy is set to E_max(c_i). If E_max(c_i) ≤ e_i, then c_i is not part of any MST when its energy is set to E_max(c_i) + 1.
